body:
## Claude review (read-only) — subject `dfd2f1575ab449507a207a2357da2a63c86e5b4f`

**Verdict: changes-requested**. Findings: 1 High, 1 Medium, 2 Low.

Note: there was no controller packet. This review is published as a PR comment, and it is read-only: no file was modified and no PR code was run. The three #491 files (`.github/workflows/inspect-demo-source-topology.yml`, `scripts/automation/inspect-demo-source-topology.mjs`, `scripts/automation/inspect-demo-source-topology.test.mjs`) were compared with the approved `fb607a287`. `git diff fb607a287 dfd2f1575` on them is **empty**, so they are not re-reviewed here. The review covers the three new source files only.

Fresh evidence gathered for this review (read-only GitHub API, inspected with my own stdlib scripts, never with the PR's code):

- The live run, artifact, job and run-attempt metadata match every pinned constant.
- Artifact `12145555014` is `expired:false`, with `expires_at` `2026-10-25T17:39:03Z`.
- The downloaded archive is 1237 bytes and its SHA-256 matches `ARCHIVE_DIGEST`.
- Its ZIP layout is: one member, flag 0x8 data descriptor, zeroed local CRC/sizes, no extra field or comment, mode `0100600`, central directory 79 bytes, EOCD consistent.
- The receipt's key sets, key order and both inventory digests match the projection in `inventory()`.
- So the **topology** path appears compatible with the real bytes, judging by reading the code.
- The real job log for job `117746872227` is **not** compatible (see F1).

### Findings

1. **High — `scripts/automation/recover-demo-topology-receipt.py:445`** (with `:446-452`)
   - _Problem:_ `ci-fingerprints` mode fails on the only log it accepts. The real log of job 117746872227 has two problems:
     - It contains ESC bytes: ANSI SGR colour codes on 6 lines, one of them inside the failing step's range. So `:445` raises `LOG_CONTROL` before any parsing.
     - It also starts with a UTF-8 BOM (`EF BB BF`). Even without the ESC check, line 0 (`﻿2026-10-18T…Z …`) fails the timestamp `fullmatch` at `:451` → `LOG_TIMESTAMP`.
   - Everything else in that log matches the parser's assumptions:
     - exactly one `##[group]Run <CI_COMMAND>` line and one `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.` line;
     - summary 714/708/3/0/3/0;
     - 3 top-level `not ok` blocks, all at `standalone-review.test.mjs` (allowlisted);
     - longest line 1300 bytes.
   - The synthetic fixture (`recover-demo-topology-receipt.test.py:113-124`) has no BOM and no colour codes. `test.py:591` asserts that ESC is rejected. So the tests encode a contract the real input breaks.
   - Fixing this needs another protected review/merge cycle, because the workflow only runs from `main`.
   - _Requested change:_
     - Strip one leading `﻿` after decoding.
     - Remove ANSI CSI/SGR sequences (`\x1b\[[0-9;]*[A-Za-z]`) before line parsing and before hashing titles, so `testTitleSha256` still maps to the plain TAP title.
     - Keep rejecting other control characters (NUL, bare ESC not part of a CSI sequence). None of the log can reach the comment except hashes, regex-bound paths and allowlisted enums, so stripping SGR does not widen what gets published.
   - _Test expectation:_
     - A fixture with a leading BOM, SGR-coloured lines both outside and inside the step, and an SGR-coloured `not ok` title should publish. Its `testTitleSha256` should equal the hash of the uncoloured title.
     - A bare/non-CSI ESC or a NUL should still be rejected.
     - Replace the current `\x1b[31mred` rejection case accordingly.

2. **Medium — `scripts/automation/recover-demo-topology-receipt.py:340-341`** (also `:61`, `:383-385`, `:596-599`)
   - _Problem:_ The diagnostic codes hide the root causes this PR exists to investigate:
     - Every transport failure becomes `HTTP_FAILED`, whatever the status (403/404/410/5xx) and whatever the stage (API vs signed storage URL). The PR description says the motivating symptom was a 403 on the storage redirect.
     - An expired artifact (`expired:true`, `:383`) and a moved `main` (`fresh_main`) both surface as the generic `INVALID_METADATA`.
   - The artifact has a hard deadline of **2026-10-25T17:39:03Z**, 7-day retention. A failed hosted run near that date would not say whether it was expiry, a storage 403 or a schema mismatch, and there may not be another review cycle before the bytes are gone.
   - _Requested change:_
     - Emit constant, non-secret codes for stage and numeric status, e.g. `API_HTTP_403` / `STORAGE_HTTP_403` (the integer `error.code` only; never the URL, headers or body).
     - Add distinct `ARTIFACT_EXPIRED` and `MAIN_MOVED` codes.
     - Mention the expiry deadline in the workflow input description or PR body.
   - _Test expectation:_
     - `HTTPError(403)` on the storage request → `STORAGE_HTTP_403`, and the signed URL is absent from stderr.
     - `expired:true` → `ARTIFACT_EXPIRED` with no archive call.
     - A second `fresh_main` mismatch → `MAIN_MOVED` with no write.

3. **Low — `scripts/automation/recover-demo-topology-receipt.py:572-574`**
   - _Problem:_ The repository is public. Any GitHub user can post a comment on #481/#492 containing the fixed `MARKER`/`CI_MARKER`, and that permanently makes the run fail with `COMMENT_CONFLICT` until a maintainer deletes the comment.
   - Fail-closed is correct, but the code cannot tell a squatted marker from a real bot-body mismatch.
   - _Requested change:_ Treat marker-bearing comments from authors other than `github-actions[bot]` as ignorable, or as a distinct `COMMENT_MARKER_FOREIGN` code. Keep exact-body matching for bot comments.
   - _Test expectation:_ A foreign user's comment containing the marker → either a publish followed by `already-published` on rerun, or `COMMENT_MARKER_FOREIGN`. A bot comment with the marker but a different body → `COMMENT_CONFLICT` (unchanged).

4. **Low — `scripts/automation/recover-demo-topology-receipt.py:584`** (interaction with `agent-team/src/bug-pipeline/comment-review-handoff.mjs:12-24`, `:336-345`)
   - _Problem:_ The published comment **cannot forge** a handoff:
     - Its body starts with `<!-- clinicos:original-demo-topology…` or `<!-- clinicos:ci-fingerprints…`, never `<!-- clinicos-review-handoff:v1 -->`.
     - Its author is `github-actions[bot]`, not the owner.
     - The JSON content is regex-bound and cannot contain `<`, backticks, `@` or URLs.
   - But `handoffFeedbackFingerprint` only excludes owner-handoff and publisher-cron comments. So this bot comment counts as new feedback on #481/#492, and dispatching during an active review round there marks that round's feedback as changed.
   - _Requested change:_ No code change needed. Add a one-line note to the workflow input description or runbook: dispatch only when no review round is in flight on the target PR, or accept the re-review.
   - _Test expectation:_ None (documentation).

### What holds up

- **Trigger and permissions:**
  - `workflow_dispatch` only, with the repository, `refs/heads/main` and `inputs.reviewed_sha == github.sha` guards repeated in Python (`context()`).
  - `main` freshness is checked again before data recovery and before writing.
  - Permissions are `contents: read`, `actions: read`, `issues: write`: the minimum needed to comment on PRs through the issues API.
  - The only action is `actions/checkout` pinned to a full SHA, `ref: github.sha`, `persist-credentials: false`.
  - Inputs reach the script through `env`, not `${{ }}` in `run:`, so there is no shell injection.
  - One concurrency group covers both modes, so dispatches are serialised.
- **Token scope:** The token is only exported to the recovery step; the test step runs without it.
- **Redirects:**
  - Automatic redirects are disabled; the single 302 `Location` is checked for https, port 443, no userinfo or fragment, and a GitHub/Azure blob host suffix.
  - The storage fetch carries no `Authorization` header and cannot redirect further.
  - Errors are constant codes; signed URLs, raw bodies and exception text never reach the console.
- **Archive:**
  - The digest and length are pinned before parsing, so zip-slip, bombs, symlinks and duplicate entries are moot for the real input.
  - The extra structural, CRC and size checks are defence in depth, and the archive is never extracted to disk.
- **JSON:** Strict JSON (duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity, recursion rejected), exact key sets at every layer, typed scalars and recomputed digests.
- **Comment safety:**
  - Comment content is fully projected from regex-bound IDs, allowlisted enums and hashes.
  - CI mode never publishes raw titles, messages, stack traces or URLs.
  - The token value is also checked as a forbidden substring.
  - Comment size limit, paginated idempotency and an exact-body/bot-author check before the "already published" path.
- **Dependencies:** Python stdlib only.
- **Tests:** The 28 offline tests are meaningful and block sockets; they cover provenance, digest, ZIP structure, schema, secrets, conflicts and redirect host rejection.
- **Simplicity:** The ZIP structure checks are heavier than a pinned digest needs, but they are contained and not worth churn.

### Limits

- I did not run the PR's tests or code, so no test results are claimed.
- I read the live GitHub metadata, downloaded the fixed artifact and job log, and inspected them only with my own stdlib scripts. The conclusion that the topology path will pass on the real bytes comes from reading the code, not from running it.
- The topology comment will publish the full demo Railway inventory (project, environment, service and instance IDs, service names, root directories, domain) on a **public** repository. AC3 of the contract explicitly asks for this. They are identifiers, not credentials, but the owner should be aware.
- I have not verified the hosted-runner behaviour on the storage redirect (the original 403).
- The CI-log byte stability between reruns, which CI-mode idempotency relies on via `fetchedBytesSha256`, is unverified.
